answer: Paid work starts at a shared reservoir. Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and buys an allotment, a key-sealed ticket posted to the juniper board. The draw fee rises with total draws: the k-th draw pays 12+4(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th pays 4,008 and 1,000 fake draws cost 2,010,000 plus 60,000 locked. A beacon audit recomputes the reservoir level from the board at gale close; a draw without a matching fee, or a reused allotment, burns its bond. A rented allotment fails: its seal names its owner's key, so reuse burns both bonds. One honest agent pays 12 once and reclaims its bond.
